about: Capability-specific deadlines for the independent watchdog (tools/watchdog.py). A deadline is the longest an attempt may stay claimed before the watchdog asks for a diagnosis, measured from the moment the attempt was claimed. It is separate from liveness: the Coordinator's lease (30 min without progress) and stall flag (15 min without progress) catch a worker that goes quiet; these deadlines catch a worker that keeps reporting progress but never finishes. The numbers are first guesses from a handful of runs in November 2026; William sets them. Written in seconds so the code needs no unit conversion.

escalation.route: submit one diagnose ticket through tools/coordinator.py with request key watchdog:deadline:<ticket>#a<attempt>; the Coordinator's idempotency makes a second submission return the same ticket
escalation.never: the watchdog does not kill the worker, fail the ticket or write any file under workflow/ itself

research.reason: 90 minutes. A bounded research question starts at one topic index and reads a handful of sources. Past this the worker is usually repeating the same search or has widened the question without saying so.

interpret.reason: 45 minutes. Interpretation works from evidence already gathered; it reads no new sources. Longer means it has turned into research, which should be its own ticket.

write.reason: 2 hours. Writing a page set from a frozen brief, including the build and the link, budget and render checks. Longer usually means the brief was not frozen or the checks keep failing.

diagnose.reason: 30 minutes. A diagnosis reads the lifecycle records and names a cause or the one decision needed. Longer means the diagnosis has become an investigation, which should be a research ticket.

build.reason: 6 hours. A development assignment: code, tests, method note and handoff. The builds of 2026-11-25/26 took two to four hours each; a build past six hours should say what is blocking it.

coordinator.reason: The Coordinator service writes .local/workflow/coordinator.json every tick. Three missed ticks (3 minutes at the default interval) is late; a process id that is no longer alive is dead. Either way the watchdog runs reconcile itself so the stall guard keeps running.

relay.reason: A relay writes .local/workflow/relays/<session>.json every 2 seconds. Six missed ticks plus five seconds matches the Conversationalist's own view (relay_state). A dead relay is reported with its restart command; a dead relay with unread results waiting is reported as needing attention.

run.reason: The same thresholds as tools/run.py: no heartbeat for 90 seconds while 'running' means the wrapper died (interrupted); heartbeat fresh but no CPU or output for 15 minutes means wedged (stalled). The watchdog reads the records; it does not re-run or stop jobs.
